tools.name: get_available_datasources
tools.title: Get available datasources
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks which datasources their Dataslayer plan lets them use, or which
ones they could add by upgrading. It returns the plan catalog: what they are ALLOWED to use,
not what they have connected. For "how many / which data sources do I have?", "my connected
sources" or "¿cuántas fuentes de datos tengo?", use get_hub_connections instead.

Returns three lists of {"id", "name"}:
- available_datasources: the datasources of the user's plan, beta ones included;
- other_datasources: datasources they could use by upgrading the plan;
- trial_datasources: usable only while a trial of a Dataslayer service lasts; access ends
  with the trial unless the user adds them to the plan or upgrades it.

Every tool that takes a datasource accepts its id or its usual name.

tools.name: get_hub_connections
tools.title: Get connected datasources
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks which or how many data sources they have connected, e.g.
"how many / which data sources do I have?", "my connected sources" or
"¿cuántas fuentes de datos tengo?". Count only the datasources whose list of connections
is not empty. For what the plan allows (trials included) use get_available_datasources;
for the accounts inside the connections use
get_available_connections_and_accounts_info_by_datasource.

Returns every datasource id with its connections; an empty list means not connected:
{
    "<datasource_id>": [{"id": "<connection id>", "is_shared": <bool>, "shared_by": "<email>"}],
    "<datasource_id>": [],
    ...
}

Use this when the user asks which metrics, dimensions or options a datasource has, e.g.
"which CTR metrics does Facebook Ads have?". Do not use it to get data: use natural_to_data.

"common"} (compact false adds each field's "description") and "options" with their possible
values. Use the returned ids as they are; never invent one. The answer can be large: narrow
it with field_type, category, search_text, common_only or limit. A search_text that finds
nothing answers a "message" saying what to try next.

tools.name: natural_to_data
tools.title: Query marketing data
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks for marketing or analytics data: metrics by dimensions for some
accounts and dates, e.g. "clicks by campaign in Facebook Ads last month". Pass the whole
request in `question`; the tool resolves the datasource, accounts, fields and dates and runs
the query. Do not use it for questions outside marketing or analytics, or only to list
datasources, fields or accounts (use the other tools for that).

One datasource and one period per call: to compare datasources (Google Ads against Facebook
Ads) or periods (September against September last year), call it once for each. When the user
refines a previous query, restate it with the change, so the accounts, metrics, dimensions and
connections they did not change stay the same.

How to read the answer:
- "success": "result" holds the table. Show the values exactly as returned, without
  rounding, splitting or combining them.
- "in-progress": the query is still running. Tell the user and give them the task_id so they
  can ask for it later (check_task_id); do not poll it on your own.
- A next_page_token in the result: show this page, and tell the user they can ask for the
  next one (get_next_paginated_result with the task_id). Do not split
  the request into smaller queries.
- "warning" with MISSING_FIELDS or "error" with MISSING_ACCOUNT: ask the user for what is
  missing instead of guessing it.
- Any other "error" or "warning": follow its next_step.

question.description: The user's data request in their own words, with the datasource, metrics, dimensions, accounts and dates they named, e.g. "clicks by campaign in Facebook Ads last month". Keep each account, property or list name exactly as the user wrote it, even when it holds a product or datasource name: "Dataslayer GA4" is a GA4 property, not the product.
question.title: Question

tools.name: dataslayer_subscription_information
tools.title: Get subscription information
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks about their Dataslayer plan, limits, usage, renewal or company,
e.g. "which is my plan?", "when is my plan renewed?", "what are my Google Sheets limits?" or
"how many users are in my company?".

Returns "account_details": email, first_name, last_name and "company" (name, owner: the user
the subscriptions belong to, users_in_company; empty when the user has no company). And
"subscriptions_details", per service the user has started (a missing service was never used):
- quota_limit (-1 means unlimited), limit_type ("query": one per call, "row": per returned
  row), limit_frequency ("daily": resets at 00:00 UTC, "monthly": resets on sub_start_day)
  and current_usage; the usage left is quota_limit - current_usage.
- plan: name, is_trial, start_date, expiration_date, billing_cycle (MONTHLY or YEARLY),
  subscription_type (custom or Stripe) and is_cancelled (true: it does not renew, but works
  until expiration_date).
- account_limit, has_blend_active, has_ai_insights_active, datasource_limit and, only when
  datasource_limit is true, datasources: the only ones usable in that service.

AI Insights (this MCP, GPTs and AI Looker Analyzer) is usable when at least one service has
has_ai_insights_active; its datasources are the union of those services' datasources, or all
of them when one of those services has datasource_limit false. Blends work the same way with
has_blend_active.

error_code.title: Error Code

next_step.description: With an error, a warning or a query still running: what to do next.
next_step.title: Next Step

company.description: Empty when the user has no company.

owner.description: Email of the user the subscriptions belong to.

current_usage.description: Usage so far: quota_limit - current_usage is left.

limit_type.description: "query": one per call; "row": one per returned row.

limit_frequency.description: "daily": resets at 00:00 UTC; "monthly": resets on sub_start_day.

sub_start_day.description: Day of the month the monthly usage resets.

tools.name: manage_alerts
tools.title: Manage AI alerts
tools.description:
Use this when the user wants to create, update, delete, list or run an AI alert, or see the
execution history of one. Pass the whole request in `question`; the tool works out the
operation and its parameters.

Structured clients may provide `request` with an empty question to save exact settings,
including active state and alert_metadata, without another model or provider lookup.
Both modes use the same account, API and stored alert IDs.

- create: needs what to watch (datasource, metric, accounts) and the condition, e.g. "alert
  me when the Facebook Ads spend of account X goes over 100". What the user leaves out is
  filled in (a name from the request, weekly frequency at the frequency's default day and
  hour, the user's timezone): the answer gives the name, frequency, scheduled_time and
  timezone used; tell the user.
- update: only the fields the user names change.
- update, delete, run and get_history need the alert id or name; ask for it when the user
  did not give one or it matches several.

An "error" carries an error_code and a next_step: follow the next_step.

question.description: The user's request about AI alerts in their own words: create, update, delete, list, run or get the history of an alert, with the alert name or id, metric, condition and schedule they named.
question.title: Question

request.description: Optional structured API request instead of natural-language inference. Use an empty question with operation get_alerts, create_alert, update_alert, delete_alert, run_alert, get_alert_history or update_history and the matching alert API fields. Identity is always taken from the authenticated session. Creation saves instructions without querying provider data; active=false pauses it.
request.title: Request

error_code.description: With an error or a warning: what went wrong, e.g. MISSING_ACCOUNT; next_step says what to do.
error_code.title: Error Code

next_step.description: With an error, a warning or a query still running: what to do next.
next_step.title: Next Step

result.description: Our API's answer: the user's alerts (a listing), the history of one, or the outcome of a change; a new alert also gives what it was created with.

message.description: Our API's message about the change.

scheduled_time.description: When it runs: the keys its frequency needs (week_day, hour, minute...).

name.description: Name the new alert was stored with.

result.title: Result

tools.name: manage_data_transfer_schedules
tools.title: Manage data transfer schedules
tools.description:
Use this when the user wants to create, update, delete, list or run a data transfer schedule,
or see the execution history of one, for these destinations: BigQuery, AWS Redshift, AWS S3,
Snowflake, Google Cloud Storage, Database, Azure SQL and Azure Storage. To list Google Sheets
or Excel schedules use get_schedules_from_user. Pass the whole request in `question`, naming
the destination.

Destination parameters, all needed to create one:
- BigQuery: project_id, dataset_id, table_id, destination_email
- AWS Redshift, Snowflake, Database, Azure SQL: table_name, connection_id
- AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Storage: upload_path, file_name, connection_id

- create: needs the data to transfer (datasource, metrics or dimensions, accounts and dates,
  as for natural_to_data), the destination parameters and the frequency (hourly, daily,
  weekly, monthly or selected hours); ask the user for what they did not give. Optional:
  the time, timezone (the user's by default), name and write mode (upsert by default; append,
  replace, or split_into_time_files for AWS S3 and Google Cloud Storage). The answer gives the
  name, schedule, timezone and write mode used; tell the user.
- update: only the fields the user names change.
- update, delete, run and get_history need the schedule id or name; ask for it when the user
  did not give one or it matches several.

An "error" carries an error_code and a next_step: follow the next_step.

tools.name: check_task_id
tools.title: Check query status
tools.description:
Use this only when the user asks whether a query they started has finished, giving its
task_id (natural_to_data returns it with status "in-progress"). Do not call it on your own
right after natural_to_data, and do not use it to start a new query. Pass the task_id exactly
as the user gave it, even when it looks wrong.

Status "success": the finished result. "in-progress": still running; tell the user to ask
again later. "warning": it finished without data. "error": its error_code says why (the query
failed, or UNKNOWN_TASK: a task_id not copied exactly or expired); follow its next_step.

tools.name: get_schedules_from_user
tools.title: Get Google Sheets and Excel schedules
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks which Google Sheets or Excel schedules they have saved. Read
only: it cannot create or change schedules. For data transfers to warehouses or storage use
manage_data_transfer_schedules. Pass destination when the user said Google Sheets or Excel.

Returns the schedules (document, type, timezone, query parameters, last execution, created
and modified dates); status "success" with an empty list means the user has none. Show every
field returned.

tools.name: natural_to_data
tools.title: Query marketing data
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks for marketing or analytics data: metrics by dimensions for some
accounts and dates, e.g. "clicks by campaign in Facebook Ads last month". Pass the whole
request in `question`; the tool resolves the datasource, accounts, fields and dates and runs
the query. Do not use it for questions outside marketing or analytics, or only to list
datasources, fields or accounts (use the other tools for that).

One datasource and one period per call: to compare datasources (Google Ads against Facebook
Ads) or periods (September against September last year), call it once for each. When the user
refines a previous query, restate it with the change, so the accounts, metrics, dimensions and
connections they did not change stay the same.

How to read the answer:
- "success": "result" holds the table. Show the values exactly as returned, without
  rounding, splitting or combining them.
- "in-progress": the query is still running. Tell the user and give them the task_id so they
  can ask for it later (check_task_id); do not poll it on your own.
- A next_page_token in the result: show this page, and tell the user they can ask for the
  next one (get_next_paginated_result with the task_id). Do not split
  the request into smaller queries.
- "warning" with MISSING_FIELDS or "error" with MISSING_ACCOUNT: ask the user for what is
  missing instead of guessing it.
- Any other "error" or "warning": follow its next_step.

question.description: The user's data request in their own words, with the datasource, metrics, dimensions, accounts and dates they named, e.g. "clicks by campaign in Facebook Ads last month". Keep each account, property or list name exactly as the user wrote it, even when it holds a product or datasource name: "Dataslayer GA4" is a GA4 property, not the product.

tools.name: dataslayer_subscription_information
tools.title: Get subscription information
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks about their Dataslayer plan, limits, usage, renewal or company,
e.g. "which is my plan?", "when is my plan renewed?", "what are my Google Sheets limits?" or
"how many users are in my company?".

Returns "account_details": email, first_name, last_name and "company" (name, owner: the user
the subscriptions belong to, users_in_company; empty when the user has no company). And
"subscriptions_details", per service the user has started (a missing service was never used):
- quota_limit (-1 means unlimited), limit_type ("query": one per call, "row": per returned
  row), limit_frequency ("daily": resets at 00:00 UTC, "monthly": resets on sub_start_day)
  and current_usage; the usage left is quota_limit - current_usage.
- plan: name, is_trial, start_date, expiration_date, billing_cycle (MONTHLY or YEARLY),
  subscription_type (custom or Stripe) and is_cancelled (true: it does not renew, but works
  until expiration_date).
- account_limit, has_blend_active, has_ai_insights_active, datasource_limit and, only when
  datasource_limit is true, datasources: the only ones usable in that service.

AI Insights (this MCP, GPTs and AI Looker Analyzer) is usable when at least one service has
has_ai_insights_active; its datasources are the union of those services' datasources, or all
of them when one of those services has datasource_limit false. Blends work the same way with
has_blend_active.

error_code.title: Error Code

current_usage.description: Usage so far: quota_limit - current_usage is left.

tools.name: manage_alerts
tools.title: Manage AI alerts
tools.description:
Use this when the user wants to create, update, delete, list or run an AI alert, or see the
execution history of one. Pass the whole request in `question`; the tool works out the
operation and its parameters.

Structured clients may provide `request` with an empty question to save exact settings,
including active state and alert_metadata, without another model or provider lookup.
Both modes use the same account, API and stored alert IDs.

- create: needs what to watch (datasource, metric, accounts) and the condition, e.g. "alert
  me when the Facebook Ads spend of account X goes over 100". What the user leaves out is
  filled in (a name from the request, weekly frequency at the frequency's default day and
  hour, the user's timezone): the answer gives the name, frequency, scheduled_time and
  timezone used; tell the user.
- update: only the fields the user names change.
- update, delete, run and get_history need the alert id or name; ask for it when the user
  did not give one or it matches several.

An "error" carries an error_code and a next_step: follow the next_step.

question.description: The user's request about AI alerts in their own words: create, update, delete, list, run or get the history of an alert, with the alert name or id, metric, condition and schedule they named.
question.title: Question

request.description: Optional structured API request instead of natural-language inference. Use an empty question with operation get_alerts, create_alert, update_alert, delete_alert, run_alert, get_alert_history or update_history and the matching alert API fields. Identity is always taken from the authenticated session. Creation saves instructions without querying provider data; active=false pauses it.

error_code.title: Error Code

next_step.title: Next Step

message.description: Our API's message about the change.

scheduled_time.description: When it runs: the keys its frequency needs (week_day, hour, minute...).

name.description: Name the new alert was stored with.

result.title: Result

tools.name: manage_data_transfer_schedules
tools.title: Manage data transfer schedules
tools.description:
Use this when the user wants to create, update, delete, list or run a data transfer schedule,
or see the execution history of one, for these destinations: BigQuery, AWS Redshift, AWS S3,
Snowflake, Google Cloud Storage, Database, Azure SQL and Azure Storage. To list Google Sheets
or Excel schedules use get_schedules_from_user. Pass the whole request in `question`, naming
the destination.

Destination parameters, all needed to create one:
- BigQuery: project_id, dataset_id, table_id, destination_email
- AWS Redshift, Snowflake, Database, Azure SQL: table_name, connection_id
- AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Storage: upload_path, file_name, connection_id

- create: needs the data to transfer (datasource, metrics or dimensions, accounts and dates,
  as for natural_to_data), the destination parameters and the frequency (hourly, daily,
  weekly, monthly or selected hours); ask the user for what they did not give. Optional:
  the time, timezone (the user's by default), name and write mode (upsert by default; append,
  replace, or split_into_time_files for AWS S3 and Google Cloud Storage). The answer gives the
  name, schedule, timezone and write mode used; tell the user.
- update: only the fields the user names change.
- update, delete, run and get_history need the schedule id or name; ask for it when the user
  did not give one or it matches several.

An "error" carries an error_code and a next_step: follow the next_step.

tools.name: check_task_id
tools.title: Check query status
tools.description:
Use this only when the user asks whether a query they started has finished, giving its
task_id (natural_to_data returns it with status "in-progress"). Do not call it on your own
right after natural_to_data, and do not use it to start a new query. Pass the task_id exactly
as the user gave it, even when it looks wrong.

Status "success": the finished result. "in-progress": still running; tell the user to ask
again later. "warning": it finished without data. "error": its error_code says why (the query
failed, or UNKNOWN_TASK: a task_id not copied exactly or expired); follow its next_step.

tools.title: Get Google Sheets and Excel schedules
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks which Google Sheets or Excel schedules they have saved. Read
only: it cannot create or change schedules. For data transfers to warehouses or storage use
manage_data_transfer_schedules. Pass destination when the user said Google Sheets or Excel.

Returns the schedules (document, type, timezone, query parameters, last execution, created
and modified dates); status "success" with an empty list means the user has none. Show every
field returned.

tools.title: Get special datasource hints
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks how to request data from a special datasource (google_trends,
google_pagespeed, google_keyword_planner, applovin, instagram_public_data,
facebook_public_data, youtube_public_data), or to know which call_type to pass to

of natural_to_data: it takes no other argument.
